Package io.webagent4j.workflow

Class WorkflowIntrospector

java.lang.Object
io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowIntrospector
public final class WorkflowIntrospector extends Object
Produces a WorkflowIntrospectionReport from an already-built, already-valid Workflow - a static complexity and safety-surface summary, computed entirely from the definition's own already-validated structure. See docs/workflow.md#static-workflow-introspection for the full contract and its relationship to WorkflowValidationReport, WorkflowExecutionPlan, and WorkflowExecutionTree.

inspect(Workflow) is strictly static: it never evaluates an IWorkflowCondition (not even IWorkflowCondition.referencedVariables() - unlike Workflow.Builder#build() /validate(), which must call that metadata method, this report needs nothing a caller-supplied condition implementation could get wrong), never calls IWorkflowActionFactory.prepare(io.webagent4j.workflow.IWorkflowVariables), never resolves or contacts a backend, browser, or network destination, and never creates a thread, executor, or Future - a WorkflowStepType.PARALLEL step's branches are inspected sequentially, in declaration order, exactly like every other container step's contents. This class is stateless and safe to share across threads: inspect(Workflow) depends on nothing but its argument, and two calls with the same workflow - and any two logically-equal, independently-built Workflow instances - always produce equal reports.

Because Workflow.Builder.build() is the only way to obtain a Workflow, every definition this class can ever receive is already known to be structurally valid and already within Workflow.MAX_CONTROL_FLOW_NESTING_DEPTH. This lets inspect(Workflow) skip every collision/diagnostic concern Workflow.Builder's own analysis must handle (an output name colliding with an existing input or an earlier step's output cannot occur in an already-valid definition) while still computing definite assignment with the exact same guard-aware rule documented on Workflow and on WorkflowIntrospectionOutput.definitelyAvailable(): this is a deliberately independent, minimal traversal - not a second call into build()/ validate() - since neither of those internal analyses is reachable from outside Workflow.

The whole traversal, including WorkflowIntrospectionReport.maximumPotentialExecutionNodes()'s worst-case computation, visits each declared step exactly a small, fixed number of times - never proportional to any declared maxIterations or branch count, never a physical unrolling. Pass 1's guard-aware definite assignment (see inspectStep(io.webagent4j.workflow.IWorkflowStep, int, io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowIntrospector.Metrics)) never copies the full accumulated declared/ definite state into a branch: inspectStep(io.webagent4j.workflow.IWorkflowStep, int, io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowIntrospector.Metrics)/inspectBranch(java.util.List<io.webagent4j.workflow.IWorkflowStep>, int, io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowIntrospector.Metrics) return only the WorkflowIntrospector.FlowDelta - the variables a step or branch itself newly introduces relative to its own entry point - which a caller merges into its own running sets in time proportional to that delta's own size, not to how many steps already precede it in the traversal. Since workflow is already known to be collision-free, a given output variable can appear in at most two deltas across the whole definition (the then/else branches of the single WorkflowStepType.CONDITIONAL that may deliberately declare it identically in both - see inspectStep(io.webagent4j.workflow.IWorkflowStep, int, io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowIntrospector.Metrics)), so the total size of every delta ever produced is O(N) in the number N of steps the definition declares. inspect(Workflow)'s total cost - traversal plus every delta merge combined - is therefore O(N), independent of how large those steps' own declared bounds (maxIterations, branch counts) are, and never proportional to how many steps already precede a given branch.

    • inspect

      public WorkflowIntrospectionReport inspect(Workflow workflow)
      Inspects workflow and returns its static WorkflowIntrospectionReport. Never throws for a valid workflow - every Workflow this method can receive is already known to be structurally valid, since Workflow.Builder.build() is the only way to obtain one.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if workflow is null
